question: Should five consecutive malformed pullAudio payloads close the Google Meet realtime bridge under the existing consecutive-input-error policy?
rationale: The implementation is internally consistent and proven, but treating malformed successful responses as cutoff-counted failures intentionally trades recovery tolerance for bounded availability when a node peer is persistently broken.

options.title: Count malformed pulls
options.body: Accept malformed payloads as input failures and retain the existing five-consecutive-error shutdown threshold.

options.title: Drop without shutdown
options.body: Reject and warn for malformed payloads without incrementing the shutdown counter, with focused tests defining that separate policy.

recommendation.title: Count malformed pulls
recommendation.body: Accept malformed payloads as input failures and retain the existing five-consecutive-error shutdown threshold.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR timeline explicitly routed the availability-risk decision here after the implementation and proof were otherwise cleared.
